name: motif_count
author: 63fb3e40
description: Counts small patterns (motifs) of 3 or 4 nodes. Size 3 is the triad census: for directed graphs the 16 types of NetworkX's triadic_census, e.g. 030T feed-forward loop (A->B->C, A->C), 030C 3-cycle, 300 mutual triangle; for undirected graphs triangles and open triads (A-B-C). Size 4 counts the six connected 4-node patterns, ignoring direction: 4_path, 4_star, 4_cycle, tailed_triangle, diamond, 4_clique. Use it for 'Which small patterns are most common?', 'How many triangles / feed-forward loops / squares are there?', 'Who is in the most triangles?' (motif) or 'How many triangles is Alice in?' (node). Works on directed and undirected graphs; weights are ignored. Returns each pattern's count, share and ratio to a random graph with as many links, triangles and transitivity (size 3), and the top_k nodes taking part most in one motif (default triangle, or 4_clique for size 4).

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

size.description: Nodes per pattern: 3 (triads, the default) or 4 (4-node patterns, direction ignored). If omitted it follows the motif.

motif.description: Optional pattern to focus on: its count and the nodes in the most copies of it. One of triangle, open_triad; for directed graphs also a triad code or name such as 030T / feed_forward_loop, 030C / cycle, 021D / out_star, 021U / in_star, 021C / chain, 300 / mutual_triangle; or a 4-node pattern: 4_path, 4_star, 4_cycle (square), tailed_triangle, diamond, 4_clique.

node.description: Optional node id: also return how many copies of each pattern this node is part of, and its rank for the focus motif. Use lookup_node to find ids.

top_k.description: How many top nodes to list for the focus motif.
